written_by_evidence: platform/workers/mini-worker/dashboard_adapter.py runs only components/metrics/refresh.py; one record = one metrics refresh (146 via dashboard-refresh/1) — the lead, 2026-10-01, for ATL-20b (exact run counts); a kind with no written_by is not attributable to any component
title: Dashboard refresh — a record of every run
note: One record per RUN of the dashboard refresh, filed by the mini worker's daily tick job (card DASH-C4, platform/workers/mini-worker/dashboard_adapter.py). The numbers on the performance page come from the always-on mini and nowhere else — no human's laptop in the loop — and this kind is the record that says so: what ran, when, whether it succeeded, whether a number actually moved, and whether that move was pushed. A refresh that DID NOT HAPPEN is readable here as a `failed` record; silence is never the answer. THE REFRESH ITSELF is components/metrics/refresh.py <run> --out --reconcile, which reads the run's source.sql, queries the warehouse and writes platform/data/metrics/<run>/{data.json, last-refresh.json}. It is spawned under scoped_env('dashboard-refresh') (WM-14), whose JOB_ENV row grants DATABASE_URL and the SUPABASE_DB_URL fallback and NO other key; PATH gets /opt/homebrew/bin because psql lives there on the mini. NO NEW SCHEDULER (the one-scheduler rule, 2026-08-27): the job rides the worker's existing 60s tick, gated by a DAY cursor at 06:15 America/New_York, so a second tick on the same NY day is a no-op and the row in platform/workers/README.md's jobs table is its declaration. The cursor advances on failure as well as success — one attempt per day, never a FAILED record every minute. PUSH ONLY ON CHANGE: the data plane is committed when a NUMBER moved, measured over the run's data directory MINUS last-refresh.json, whose refreshed_at moves on every rerun by design; on an unchanged day the record is written and rides the next push. NO CREDENTIAL EVER APPEARS: the connection string's exact value is scrubbed out of every captured line before it is logged or filed. Item id = the dashboard run name (a runs/<run>/ folder, discovered — never named in the worker, workspace rule 7), so a second brand is a second source.sql and a second item id. Several records exist per run and the LATEST BY `created` WINS; the history is the append-only record, never an edit.

verdict_fields.note: exactly one per record; reserved so a later index or status event can join this kind without changing what a refresh record means
the dashboard run name; equals the record's item id

`failed` covers BOTH named failure modes and they are told apart by `failure`: a missing credential (the refresh never started) and a non-zero exit from refresh.py (it started and did not finish clean, which includes a --reconcile mismatch). Neither ever kills the worker's tick.

which wall it hit, as a token a reader can count on. Named rather than left to prose because 'the env var is not set' and 'the warehouse disagreed with itself' are different problems with different owners.
the failure in words, including what to do about it
refresh.py's exit code; null when it was never spawned (missing credential). 124 = timed out, 125 = could not be run.
did a NUMBER move — the data directory's diff MINUS last-refresh.json, whose refreshed_at moves on every rerun by design. This is the only thing that authorises a push. Always false on a failed run.
up to 20 repo-relative paths that moved — pointers, never content

was the change committed and pushed. false with changed=true means the data moved and the push failed or was not asked for (a CLI run pushes nothing by design) — the two are different facts and are never collapsed.

present only when the record claimed a push that then failed. The record is filed BEFORE the push so it rides the same commit as the numbers; a push that fails is corrected on disk by the same run, seconds later and before any reader could have seen it, rather than leaving a claim nobody checked. Not an exception to the append-only rule — no LATER record ever edits an earlier one.
the America/New_York calendar day this tick was cursored to (YYYY-MM-DD). The cursor key: one attempt per day, and a second tick on the same day is a no-op.
the exact refresh invocation, as words — never a shell string to re-run blind
repo-relative directory the run wrote (platform/data/metrics/<run>/) — a POINTER; the viewer reads the numbers there and never from this record
which of the credential names the scoped environment actually carried — NAMES ONLY, never values. What a reader checks first when a refresh fails.

the run's last-refresh.json in summary — refreshed_at, cutoff and row counts (orders, days, spend_days, months, fulfillment_rate). Counts and a cutoff, never rows. null on a failed run, and a stated absence when the file could not be read.

the refresh's own output, tail-trimmed, with the credential's value scrubbed out. A diagnostic — the full text is in worker.log. WM-6: the log rides with the verdict, so a reader never has to hold a record and a log file side by side to find out what happened.
present only when the 16KB cap forced a shed, naming what was dropped. The log sheds first and nothing else sheds at all.
